Priya — quick business note from our side: we’re willing to accept a narrow OSS carveout (for upstream-licensed components) provided the carveout:

- Is limited to components that are not modified by the customer and where Redwood was the distributor;
- Still requires the customer to provide timely notice and cooperate on defense; and
- Includes a clear cap tied to the Order Form (not unlimited).

All — reviewed BioMosaic’s redline. Below are two clean snippets we can present, with rationale and an ops checklist. I’ve attached a plain-text excerpt (proposed_indemnity_snippet.txt) and will drop the updated Order Form v3 once we agree on direction.

Option A (Redwood fallback — lean):
"Redwood agrees to defend and indemnify Customer from third-party claims to the extent such claims arise solely from Redwood's breach of a patent or copyright that covers materials provided by Redwood for Customer's use, provided that Customer: (i) notifies Redwood promptly; (ii) gives Redwood sole control of the defense and settlement; and (iii) does not modify the accused materials. Redwood's indemnity obligation shall not extend to claims attributable to Customer modifications, Customer content, or third-party integrations. Redwood's aggregate liability under this section shall not exceed the total paid by Customer under the applicable Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim."

Option B (compromise — OSS carveout with conditions):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood shall have no indemnity obligation for third-party claims arising from: (a) Open Source Software governed by an OSI-approved license (\"OSS\") incorporated in the deliverables unless such OSS was distributed by Redwood under a separate written agreement that grants rights sufficient for Customer's intended use; or (b) components for which Customer has altered or augmented the code. For OSS where Redwood is the distributor, Redwood's indemnity is conditioned on Customer providing: (i) an SBOM or SPDX manifest for the affected component; (ii) evidence of the version and checksum; and (iii) reasonable cooperation in Redwood's defense. In such cases Redwood's liability shall be capped as set forth in the Order Form."

Ops checklist (evidence needed if Option B applies):
- SPDX/SBOM or license manifest (preferred formats: SPDX v2.2 or CycloneDX)
- Model fingerprint/hash and model version metadata
- Proof of distribution chain showing Redwood as distributor (if applicable)
- Access to runtime logs showing model invocation in scope of the claim

Rationale: Option A preserves our standard commercial indemnity posture; Option B is acceptable for strategic accounts (like BioMosaic) if we tie the indemnity to documentary evidence and keep a clear cap and defense/control mechanics.

Next steps proposal: share both snippets with BioMosaic Tue morning, request their preference, and schedule a 30-min legal/sales call Tue afternoon to finalize. If they push for broader provenance requirements, escalate to product for a quick confirmation of how much provenance we can provide without leaking internal model ops.

Attachments referenced: proposed_indemnity_snippet.txt
